description: Aficionado de la radioastronomía y experimentador con hardware y software. Este team busca personas con conocimientos en linux, estadística, electrónica y telecomunicaciones.
summary:
Astra Sleuth is a browser-based application built for the NASA Challenge 2026 that analyzes 20 to 45 years of monthly satellite and reanalysis data to determine whether a change in an Earth variable is a real statistical trend or merely natural variability.

Long environmental records are inherently noisy a warm decade, a wet season, or a single El Niño event can easily mimic a trend on a simple chart. To solve this, Astra Sleuth pairs an interactive 3D globe and charting interface with rigorous statistical tests (such as the Mann-Kendall test with autocorrelation correction and Sen's slope), removing seasonal cycles to deliver robust, client-side significance testing. Requiring no backend infrastructure or API keys, the application translates complex statistical outputs into plain-language verdicts at two distinct levels (Student and Scientist), empowering learners, educators, and researchers to explore climate data with confidence.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Astra Sleuth is a browser-based Earth-system trend detective. Users pick a climate variable, select a point or region (or two regions in Dipole Mode) on a MapLibre 3D globe with NASA GIBS layers, choose a year range and season, and run multidecadal analysis on 20–45 years of NASA POWER and NOAA ERDDAP data (fetched in parallel 5-year chunks with retries, plus NASA Giovanni CSV import). A Rust with WebAssembly engine inside a Web Worker removes seasonal cycles and computes Seasonal Mann–Kendall, Hamed–Rao AR correction, Sen's Slope, Pettitt abrupt shift dates, and a Significance Horizon curvemdelivering plain-language verdicts, 4 one-click presets (Panama Canal ENSO dipole, Gulf of Panama upwelling, Wisconsin wildfire AOD, Arctic vs. Sahel), and HTML/CSV/JSON exports.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Zero backend servers or API keys, instant client-side WASM speed, Student / Scientist detail levels, and EN / ES interfaces. It empowers students, educators, and regional analysts to separate real trends from natural noise and explore how one driver pushes distant regions in opposite directions.

Creativity & Factors Considered
Uniquely pairs a live Hamed–Rao autocorrelation toggle(preventing false positives) with Dipole comparison and significance Horizon curves, using colorblind-safe palettes and strict handling of seasonality and missing values.

Tools & Hardware Used
Rust, WebAssembly, TypeScript, Node.js, MapLibre GL (3D globe), uPlot, NASA POWER, GIBS, Giovanni, NOAA ERDDAP. An initial 1.694 GHz GOES-19 L-band dish prototype built in Panama.

GitHub: https://github.com/ArlandBarrera/astra-sleuth
